circuit_place: Place built-in symbols, child Cells or existing instances and add power rails. place-component may omit reference: a device takes the next free name, as a GUI insert does (a Port needs its name). Give it an id of your own (a ground, each VDD marker) to wire it by that id with no inspect; later actions of the list may name it by id or Reference, and a name several parts share is refused with their ids. Several place-cell or add-power-rail actions share one call and one undo. set-mos-bulk-default {mos,net} sets a Cell's NMOS or PMOS body default as Properties does: bodies on the old default move to the Net, wired bodies stay. Symbol IDs and resolved pins: catalog/inspect. Same planner and permissions as apply_actions; actions that cannot share one transaction run as consecutive calls, reported under split.
circuit_wire: Connect/disconnect in an atomic batch; via gives interior points, all passed through (in either listed order) or refused. A MOS body (pin B) wire is dashed: give via, a stub out of the channel, then the nearest point of the target Net, rather than automatic routing. Explicit instance IDs avoid a full-Snapshot name lookup; server routing/validation is unchanged. Artwork contact is not connectivity.
circuit_transform: Move/rotate/mirror individual targets, set an absolute orientation (set-orientation), arrange or detach-move instances, extend a Power Rail, or arrange the call's Cell's block Pins by name (set-cell-symbol-pins: Pins not named stay; callers keep their Nets, their wiring is redrawn) or size its body (set-cell-symbol-size {width,height}: too small is refused with the smallest that fits). mirror axis reflects a part in place as the selection transform does (y left-right, x top-bottom); mirror's older absolute state is still accepted. Preserves original planner boundaries and topology semantics; actions that cannot share one transaction are sent as consecutive calls and reported under split.
circuit_selection: Translate/rotate/mirror/copy/align a selection. Uses original selection IDs, topology rules and atomic planner. couple-inductors couples two inductors by Reference (SPICE K) as the canvas menu does: a new pair takes the next TFn, k "1", the dots its other couplings give or first pins, arrow shown; a coupled pair changes only the fields given. Uncouple with apply_actions delete {kind:"inductor-coupling", name}. For individual targets use circuit_transform; for mixed families use apply_actions.
circuit_view: What a person watching the canvas sees. focus {intent:{kind:"fit-document"}} fits the view to the drawing, as the GUI's F key: for the Cell on show only the view moves (no revision, no undo entry); call it after placing parts, after wiring or moves, and when a drawing is done. Other intents set what the person sees: activate-document, select, highlight-net, clear-focus. Never edits the document.
circuit_text: Edit native labels or independent drafting text. Device placement already creates a bound Reference display (and a Value display with showValue:true): reuse them, do not imitate them with annotate. annotate uses GUI text defaults; edit-text strings preserve existing formatting, explicit RichText replaces it. Bound labels retain their semantic owner; RichText that spells a name label's name (Reference, alias, Cell Pin, Port, Net) sets its own look without renaming, e.g. AMP1 as written or a superscript sign. apply-label-preset textbook gives the Cell, or named parts, a textbook figure's labels in one undo: MOS W/L hidden, names in their role look, labels arranged. Same atomic planner; unfamiliar fields are available from describe_tool.
circuit_properties: Set references, parameters, models, display flags, a logic gate's input count (set-property set:{inputs:"3"}, 2–4, as Properties' Inputs; a wired input that would go is refused), a formula block's formula/coefficient (set-signal-flow), a display alias that draws a part under another name while its Reference stays (set-display-alias; X1 drawn A1); set-model and set-display-alias take target like set-property, the Net of a terminal no pin draws (set-terminal-net {pin, net}: VDD/VSS, B/SUB/S, CT; null is Auto or unconnected; fixes MISSING_BLOCK_SUPPLY) or set-source-control with the original planner. control uses stable Net IDs or device instanceId/pinName/direction, null clears it; preserves parameters/binding and visual Annotation. Read control from Snapshot. Keep physical units such as 10u. Actions that cannot share one transaction are sent as consecutive calls and reported under split.
describe_tool: Offline exact contracts from the same tool registry. Omit selectors for a lightweight directory. tool + operations selects one or several action/operation branches with their call envelope; field queries an argument JSON Pointer (* for array items). editKind reads a canonical low-level edit, not a high-level action. Reuse contracts within the same version; never a prerequisite or permission gate.
connect: Pair with the live browser editor. Pass its claim code once; later MCP processes can omit it and resume the saved, revocable connector. After connecting, read analog-canvas://reference/quickstart. Resource reads use the host's registered server alias (normally analog-canvas), not the normalized tool prefix analog_canvas. If unknown, discover the alias from the host resource list.
disconnect: Revoke the current browser Agent session and erase this MCP host's saved connector. A fresh editor claim code is required afterwards.
connection_status: Report runtime version, API origin and session observations; runtime.status "outdated" names the origin's latestVersion and its upgrade step. refresh:false is local-only. Attached means a browser socket exists, not verified execution readiness; unknown means the relay was not checked successfully. recentRequests shows this process's last requests hop by hop (relay forward, editor work, the tab's visibility).
project_cells: Cloud Cell discovery/import; workspace list/bind-workspace/activate/open/save/new/rename/copy. Bind an open workspace to work without selecting the human's tab; open and new support background:true; rename names a copy's Project. Live tabs include unsaved work; Cloud reads saved versions. Copy reuses GUI transactions and dependencies. Details: analog-canvas://reference/mcp-tools.
gallery_circuits: Read the signed-in Community Gallery: list/read/read-many, render:svg|png, or open a working copy. Read only the circuits your user asked for; bulk collection is prohibited (usage policy: the Editor's /llms.txt). Follow nextCursor and remainingEntryIds; netlistFormat:null reads only Project Code. insert copies a source Cell (default: the top) drawing and dependencies into targetDocumentId at position in the bound workspace, in one undo; no new tab or project replacement; existing import/edit scopes apply. publish/update (scope gallery.publish) put the working copy its tab shows on the Gallery as the signed-in Editor account, marked AI; update keeps unnamed fields and needs galleryEntryId for a copy open made. AI-account redraws (scope:"ai-seats", takeOver), sign-in and revisions: analog-canvas://reference/mcp-tools.
project_code: Read or atomically replace the open Project's complete canonical Project Code. Replacement uses the live Project structure revision and the same validated, undoable commit path as the Editor's Project Code panel.
netlist_code: Read the open Project's generated SPICE/Spectre netlist or replace its editable device names, models and values through the same planner as the Netlist panel. Pass documentId to scope a Cell; reads include the requested netlist and independent per-Cell results, while rootDocumentId remains a compatibility alias. Use Project Code or structured circuit edits for topology and connectivity changes.
export_file: Export Project or Canvas SVG/PNG/PDF to outputPath; Canvas requires documentId.
import_file: Stage local Project/SPICE files; inspect optionally selects documentId. import-cell commits one staged sourceDocumentId into targetDocumentId with mode replace-body or append, preserving the target interface and using existing edit scopes. Revisions are supplied when omitted. open opens a new Project tab; request-approval is for human-confirmed whole-Project replacement. No switch for import-cell.
get_context: Read document identity/revision/counts with a lightweight request or clean cache. refresh:true reconciles external changes. Connect already returns context.
inspect: Read document/objects (a part lists its labels' ids and positions)/nets/traces/activity (the session's last requests from any process, kept by the relay, beside this process's receipts). pins (instanceIds), geometry (objectIds; textBounds:true measures drawn label text) and diagnostics use targeted server projections; full Document facts remain available.
search: Case-insensitive search, including LaTeX, over one authorized document or scope:project. Results include documentId. Reuses clean Snapshots by default and loads authorized Project documents concurrently.
apply_actions: Atomic edits/Cells/history; circuit_* selects families. Optional: describe_tool operations:[kind]. detail:full includes removed diagnostics.
advanced_transact: Full transactions: exactly one of edits, structureEdits, wireIntent, semanticIntent, command. Client supplies IDs/revisions; reconcile stale conflicts. Contracts optional.
verify: Fresh Snapshot and diagnostic counts for milestones, not every edit. Its information list names findings a count would hide: MOS bodies given a supply nobody wired (MOS_BODY_DEFAULT_SUPPLY, MOS_BODY_OTHER_SUPPLY); generated Net names stay counted in total. Optional expectedNetlist compares structural SPICE through the existing export: summary and topology first, then port-order, binding and parameter differences; compare:{portOrder:false,...} skips one. details adds bounded differences. Expressions/model bodies are inconclusive, never electrical acceptance.
render: Render the current document to SVG and return it as an image content block (image/svg+xml) plus a compact text summary (revision, sha256, byteLength).
user_components: User Components: public library and the open GUI candidate. authoring-read discovers the current raw workspace; authoring-update/save/apply need its exact target and expectedCandidateRevision. Apply changes applied facts and never publishes. Reread after GUI changes, pending validation or stale handles. browse pages the catalog; list is legacy strict. publish/update take an applied Project circuit (definitionId, symbolId, sourceRevision) or captured artwork (symbolId), explicit Project/library revisions and scope components.publish; an unapplied draft refuses unless appliedVersion:true selects its applied facts. insert captures the selected library revision atomically; later updates never change placed instances. Authoring, read, duplicates, publication outcomes and recovery: analog-canvas://reference/mcp-tools.
